_README: Method-selection assistant (§30) and which-instrument guidance (§38). Every leaf MUST declare cannotTell — the renderer refuses to show a recommendation without its limits. OrigaMaster technique names are recorded because that is what appears on this group's instrument screen; they come from the OrigaLys OrigaFlex catalogue, not from memory. No instrument specifications are recorded anywhere here.

start.question: What do you want to investigate?
start.hint: Pick the question you actually have, not the technique you already know how to run. The right method follows from the question — and every method below has real limits, stated on its card.

options.label: Charge-storage behaviour
options.detail: How much charge does it store, and by what mechanism?

options.label: Resistance or kinetics
options.detail: What is limiting the rate — contact, electrolyte, charge transfer, diffusion?

options.label: Open-circuit behaviour
options.detail: What does the cell do when nothing is imposed on it?

options.label: Long-term cycling performance
options.detail: How does it behave over many cycles, or at different rates?

options.label: A time-dependent response to a step
options.detail: Apply a step and watch the system relax.

q_storage.question: How do you want to look at it?
q_storage.hint: CV and GCD answer different questions about the same electrode. CV maps the response across a potential range; GCD measures what you actually get at a defined current.

options.label: Across a potential range
options.detail: Where does current flow, and is it capacitive or faradaic?

options.label: At a defined current
options.detail: How much capacity or capacitance, and how efficiently?

q_step.question: Which quantity do you want to control?

options.label: Control the potential
options.detail: Step the potential, watch the current decay.

options.label: Control the current
options.detail: Step the current, watch the potential move.

leaf_cv.summary: Sweep the potential back and forth and record the current. The workhorse for seeing where charge storage happens across a potential range.
canTell: Where in the potential window current flows, and whether it is reversible
Whether the response looks capacitive (rectangular) or faradaic (peaked)
How the response scales with scan rate — the basis of b-value analysis
Whether the electrolyte's stability window is being exceeded at the extremes
cannotTell: The capacity or capacitance you would actually get in a device — GCD at a defined current is the honest measure of that
A mechanism on its own. CV shape depends on electrode material, electrolyte, concentration, geometry, scan rate, cell configuration and background current
Whether apparent peak separation is slow electron transfer or simply uncompensated resistance, without independent evidence
leaf_cv.caution: Peak separation is affected by uncompensated resistance as well as by kinetics. Measure the solution resistance independently — the high-frequency intercept of an impedance spectrum — before reading kinetics into it.

leaf_gcd.summary: Apply a constant current and record the potential. The measurement that most directly answers 'how much does it store, and how efficiently'.
canTell: Capacity or capacitance at a stated current density
Coulombic efficiency, from the discharge and charge capacities of the same cycle
The IR drop at each current reversal, and therefore the ohmic loss
Whether the curve is linear (capacitive) or plateaued (battery-type)
cannotTell: Which process is limiting the rate — that needs impedance
Anything reliable if the active material mass or the voltage window is not accurately known
A comparable number across studies unless the current density, cell configuration, mass basis and IR-drop convention all match
leaf_gcd.instrument: Battery cycler for long runs; workstation for single cycles and small currents
leaf_gcd.caution: Whether the IR drop is included in ΔV changes the capacitance you calculate. State the convention every time you report one — the GCD simulator in this module lets you see how much difference it makes.

leaf_eis.summary: Apply a small alternating signal across a range of frequencies and measure the complex impedance. Separates processes by their characteristic timescales.
canTell: The ohmic resistance of the cell, from the high-frequency intercept
That processes with different time constants are present, and roughly where they sit in frequency
Whether the low-frequency response looks diffusion-like
How any of the above changes with state of charge, temperature or cycle number
cannotTell: Which physical process an equivalent-circuit element corresponds to. More than one circuit can usually fit the same spectrum, and a good fit is not evidence of physical meaning
Anything trustworthy if the system drifted during the measurement — the low-frequency points take the longest and are the first to be corrupted
Anything meaningful if the perturbation was too large for the response to stay linear
leaf_eis.instrument: Electrochemical workstation (some cyclers offer it — check your model)
leaf_eis.origalys: Pot. Dynamic EIS  /  Gal. Dynamic EIS
leaf_eis.caution: Check linearity, stationarity and causality before interpreting a spectrum. The practical test for linearity is simple: halve the amplitude and confirm the spectrum does not change.

leaf_ocp.summary: Impose nothing and watch the potential over time. Usually the first measurement of any session.
canTell: Whether the cell has equilibrated and is ready to measure
Whether the reference electrode is behaving — persistent drift is often a reference problem, not a material one
Whether the cell is leaking, shorted or still wetting
cannotTell: Anything quantitative about capacity, kinetics or resistance
The equilibrium potential, if the measurement was simply stopped too early — slow drift and true equilibrium look alike over a short window
leaf_ocp.instrument: Electrochemical workstation, and most cyclers as a rest step
leaf_ocp.caution: A stable OCP is a precondition for a meaningful measurement, not a formality. Starting a CV or an impedance sweep on a drifting cell breaks the stationarity those methods assume.

leaf_ca.summary: Step the potential and record the current decay.
canTell: How quickly the system responds to a potential change
Whether the current decay is consistent with diffusion-limited behaviour
The charge passed, by integrating the current
cannotTell: A diffusion coefficient without a model whose assumptions genuinely apply to your geometry and system
Anything clean in the first instants, where the double-layer charging transient dominates and can swamp the faradaic response

leaf_cp.summary: Step the current and record the potential response. The mirror image of chronoamperometry.
canTell: How the potential responds to an imposed current
The IR contribution, from the immediate step at the moment the current changes
Transition times, where the potential moves sharply
cannotTell: Anything separating ohmic from kinetic polarisation unless sampling is fine enough to resolve the IR step
Rate capability on its own — that needs a series of currents
leaf_cp.instrument: Electrochemical workstation, or a cycler for longer steps

leaf_cycler.technique: Battery cycler — rate capability and long-term cycling
leaf_cycler.summary: Many channels running constant-current schedules over days to months. The right instrument for anything involving hundreds or thousands of cycles.
canTell: Capacity retention against cycle number
Rate capability across a series of C-rates
Coulombic efficiency cycle by cycle
Formation behaviour and first-cycle irreversible capacity
cannotTell: Why performance is fading — that needs impedance, post-mortem characterisation, or both
Anything about a single electrode, unless the cell was deliberately built with a reference
Anything trustworthy if the active mass entered on the instrument was wrong
leaf_cycler.origalys: Single Charge or Discharge  /  Gal. Charge and Discharge Cycle
leaf_cycler.caution: GITT and PITT sit between the two instruments: whether you run them on a cycler or a workstation depends on the pulse magnitude, the timescale and what your particular instrument supports. Check your own model rather than assuming.
